title: A Christmas Carol at PAC NYC #achristmascarol #pacnyc #michaelcerveri...
transcript: Last night, I saw one of the biggest collections of indoor lanterns ever. Yes, A Christmas Carol at the Perelman Arts Center in FiDi. This version by Jack Thorne directed by Matthew Warchus actually played on Broadway in 2019, but I imagine they had to reconfigure parts of it to suit this new venue. That said, it's clear why the production won a bunch of Tony Awards. The immersive and whimsical staging, plus all the lovely design flourishes, keep the production visually engaging the entire time. I love the way the production integrates music and how the ensemble effortlessly moves between distinct characters and a narrating body. The cast is remarkably commanding and intuitive, knowing exactly when to be terse and when to be a little more saccharine. Highlights for me were Crystal Lucas-Perry as the Ghost of Christmas Present, Julia Knitel as Belle, and of course, Michael Cerveris as Ebenezer Scrooge. For a story that everyone already knows, this version feels sufficiently fresh and inspired, while exemplifying why the story has become a timeless classic. As you might expect, this is only running through the holiday season. With that, another program for my collection.
